name: Assault Runner
instructions: Step onto the curved, non-motorized treadmill belt and start with short, light steps, since the belt only moves when driven by your own foot strike.
Drive your feet backward beneath your hips to accelerate the belt to the desired speed, keeping your torso upright and avoiding overstriding.
Because the belt has no motor, an assault runner requires more muscular effort than a standard treadmill at the same perceived pace, making it effective for interval training.
